product: Crimson Wildflower Maxi Skirt (pilot, elastic waistband)
README: The waistband of the pilot skirt is NOT measured yet. Every number under `assumed` is an assumption, not a measurement. When the founder has the tape numbers, fill `measured` (copy `measuredTemplate`) and run `BAND=measured serverdrape/drape.sh`: nothing else changes, and drapes cached with other band numbers are re-run automatically. Fields: `relaxedGirthCm` = the band's full girth lying relaxed (flat width x 2); `stretchedGirthCm` = the full girth pulled to its comfortable maximum; `hemSweepCm` = the full hem girth (flat hem width x 2); `gradePerSizeCm` = how much the band changes per chart size if only the sample size is measured (null = the chart's waist step, 5 cm per AU size). What each field DOES: relaxedGirthCm sets the band's rest girth per size (drives the drape); stretchedGirthCm sets the band's stiffness via the stretch ratio (drives the drape; mapping in band_model.py, ASSUMED); hemSweepCm is a CHECK only (drape.sh warns when the reconstructed garment's hem differs by more than 5 %).

assumed.note: ASSUMED, not measured. relaxed(size) = chart waist(size) + offsetCm when graded, else the fixed girth for every size; stretched = relaxed x stretchRatio (per variant, else the default). The band's tension stiffness relative to the fabric is elasticToFabricStiffness x (stiffnessReferenceStretchRatio - 1) / (stretchRatio - 1): ASSUMED mapping and ASSUMED constant.

W-0.why: band relaxed = body waist of the size: loose at the low-rise line

W-6.why: typical elastic skirt band, about 6 cm under the body waist (assumption, not a measurement)

ONE-70.why: one band for every size (the 'every size hangs from the same band' hypothesis of REFINEMENT R3)

W-6-s1.25.why: W-6 with a firm band (stretches 25 %): twice as stiff

W-6-s2.0.why: W-6 with a very stretchy band (stretches 100 %): half as stiff
